Soon, the smell of sizzling rations quickly spread, drawing curious glances from the freed slaves nearby.
Meanwhile, Russel, the scout, was already inspecting the perimeter.
He greeted Jonas, who was guarding the wall as expected, since it was also his job back in New Haven Shelter-45.
He then started looking around, and he caught cracks in the walls and weak points near the gate.
Without hesitation, he headed to the warehouse that Kai had pointed out and started rummaging through supplies until he found coils of barbed wire.
"Perfect," he muttered.
Using scattered stones and debris as anchors, Russel reinforced the weak spots, placing the barbed wire into improvised barriers.
Within an hour, the holes and cracks in the shelter’s defenses were filled with the help of a few other people who had noticed what he was trying to do.
Kai smiled as he observed all this quietly, impressed by how quickly the group adapted.
Amer served healthier meals, Russel was fortifying defenses, while Claire and the others seemed to be cataloguing weapons and energy cells.
Soon, Kai, Jonas, and Aurora were looking at the crop samples on the table...
"These crops..." Aurora muttered as she saw four baskets containing four different crops...
"These are what the slaves were forced to grow," Kai said.
"I’ve already appraised them..."
Kai then shared what he had found out...
He pointed first to the potato‐like tuber with violet and orange spots.
[ Mutagenic Root ]
[ Grade: Hazardous Material
Description: A genetically altered tuber designed to produce unstable toxins.
When consumed, it can trigger mutations in organic tissue or destabilize biological systems. ]
[ Note: Not intended for food.
Harvested as raw material for bioweapon development.
Prolonged exposure may weaken the human immune system. ]
Aurora frowned as she saw these...
Kai then moved to the second basket.
Inside were thick, pale stalks with spherical ends...
[ Disruptive Stem ]
[ Grade: Hazardous Material
Description: A modified stalk crop engineered to interfere with human gene stability.
Prolonged contact or ingestion can disrupt gene mutations, weakening or nullifying enhancement serums. ]
[ Note: Survivors exposed may lose the benefits of specific gene enhancements temporarily. ]
Aurora’s eyes widened.
"That’s... dangerous.
If this spreads, it could undo everything the serums gave us."
Kai nodded.
"Exactly.
They’re cultivating weapons meant to cripple us.
Anyway, a few of them nearby aren’t a big issue.
Also, I don’t think those with Alpha Gene Enhancements will have issues.
Jonas tried...
I think only the low-quality ones will be affected."
He then pointed to the third basket.
This one contained oily pods...
[ Oil Pod ]
[ Grade: Industrial Material
Description: A crop designed to produce synthetic oil.
Not edible for humans.
When processed, it serves as fuel and lubricant. ]
[ Note: Survivors cannot consume this safely.
However, it may be repurposed as crude fuel for generators or mechanical repairs. ]
"Smells like engine grease..." Aurora muttered as she recalled the Artillery in New Haven Shelter-45.
Finally, Kai gestured to the fourth basket.
Inside were small, thorny tubers...
[ Sustenance Vine ]
[ Grade: Hazardous Material ]
[ Description: A vine engineered to produce watery sap.
When consumed, the juice fills satiety and prevents starvation, but it gradually poisons the body, weakening organs and causing long‐term damage.
The leaves can also be eaten, offering temporary relief from hunger while accelerating the toxic effect. ]
[ Note: Survivors relying on it will eventually suffer organ failure or collapse from cumulative poisoning. ]
Aurora frowned at this as she realized that this crop was what kept the slaves alive.
However, she looked at Kai, confused by what he was trying to show her.
"Wait...
Do you want me to cultivate these plants?"

chapters.title: Chapter 175: The World News
paragraphs: A few hours earlier, before the alarms and the chaos, Mei had been sitting quietly near the entrance of the shelter, playing with Desmond...
It was the name she had given to the golden retriever. At this time, Desmond wagged his tail happily, rolling onto his back as she rubbed his belly.
Ever since she had found him inside the shelter, she had taken care of him, fed him, and kept him close.
Naming him had felt natural. Desmond was hers, and she had every right to give him an official name.
"I wonder why you’re here?" Mei murmured softly, scratching behind his ears.
"This was an A.I. soldiers’ base meant for cultivating those four crops. There shouldn’t be a dog here at all."

This was indeed a mystery that no one could answer. Even the previous slaves had never noticed this dog. Probably because they were busy and staying at the eastern building... or perhaps, the dog was a mystical creature that had suddenly appeared.
In any case, Desmond just barked at her, as if answering her. Anyway, though his presence was strange that it was almost unsettling, she didn’t mind it at all.
"Whatever..."
Even if it was questionable to have a loyal, living creature here, Desmond was already hers.
She then looked at the horizon and sighed.
"Still... I wonder why the enemies aren’t attacking yet."
It was a thought that had been gnawing at her.
Since Kai and the others had cut off the supplies and halted production of the four crops from the A.I. bases, retaliation was expected.
Kai had warned everyone to stay alert. Yet, for now, there were no signs of enemies at all.
To distract herself, Mei opened the World Chat, a feature only available to survivors who had reached Level 20 and above.
She remembered when only three people had been in the chat. Now, the screen was filled with names, messages, and arguments.
The world was finally getting much stronger Survivors.
Then, the chat scrolled quickly despite having a limit of 3 chats per day...
[ Liza: Anyone else from Haven‐2? I keep seeing names but no one’s answering me. ]
[ Tomas: Haven‐22 here. Don’t worry, you’re not alone. ]
[ Riko: Wait... why is everyone Haven? Isn’t this supposed to be WORLD chat? ]
[ System: Darius has entered the chat. ]
[ Darius: Uh... hi. First time here. I just reached Level 20. I’m from Grid‐07. Anyone else? ]
Mei smiled. She couldn’t help but feel happy about these new Level 20 people. It was impressive that they were surviving well enough to reach this point.
[ Hana: Haven‐8 here. Welcome! ]
[ Victor: New Haven-45 here. You’ll get used to this place. ]
[ Darius: Thanks... but why do I only see Haven shelters talking? Is this normal? ]
[ Owen: Yeah, I was wondering the same thing. ]
[ Eliza: No... I’m from Grid‐12, but it feels like 90% of people here are Haven. Weird. Is it easy mode in that region? You guys are lucky. ]
[ Joseph: Maybe the others don’t bother talking. ]
[ Claire: Or maybe the system’s broken. JK. ]
Mei chuckled softly. It reminded her of the early days... confusion, complaints, and jokes. Survivors were the same everywhere.
Then a new line appeared. No system chime this time. Just a name everyone recognized.
[ Kai: It’s not broken. I think this chat isn’t global. It only covers the Republic of Mavis. ]
The tone shifted instantly.
[ Renji: Oh... Kai’s here. ]
[ Hana: Kai? Amazing... So can you explain this mess. Why does WORLD chat feel like Haven chat? Is your region that noob? And what is this Mavis? ]
Kai’s reply came.

[ Kai: Not sure about the dominance of Haven Region. But for Mavis... That’s where we are. It’s part of the Versailles Continent. Everything we see here... shelters, rankings, even this chat. I think it is limited to this republic. ]
Confusion erupted again.
[ Owen: Republic of... what? ]
[ Connie: Don’t mess with us. This is WORLD chat. ]
[ Claire: LoL. ]
Kai didn’t hesitate and shared his thoughts.

[ Kai: I believe that we can think of it as a world within a world. The system calls it World Chat, but it’s restricted. It only connects survivors inside Mavis. This is what I believe... Also, this is my last chat of the day... See you tom. ]
[ Joseph: That makes no sense. Why restrict us? ]
[ Mei: Maybe to keep order. If communication were global, chaos would spread faster than survival strategies. Restriction is intentional. ]
Mei stroked Desmond’s fur, smiling faintly as she finished replying. Kai already mentioned this to them during a meeting.
[ Tomas: So how many regions are in Mavis? ]
[ Mei: According to Sir Kai, we have six. Storm, Grid, Frontier, Origin, Novel, and Haven. ]
[ Eliza: And the Leaderboard? ]
[ Mei: Most likely restricted too. Kai told me that even if he’s ranked number one, he believed that that’s only within Mavis. If there are other nations, then might have their own leaderboards. ]
The chat shifted after Kai’s silence.
[ Owen: Did anyone else see that flying fortress heading west? Looked massive, like a moving city in the sky. ]
[ Hana: Yeah, I caught a glimpse. Thought it was a storm cloud until the drones started circling it. ]
[ Vera: If it’s heading west... that means Frontier, or is it Origin Region. Do you think it’s going to hunt humans? ]
Mei’s hand froze on Desmond’s fur. A flying fortress? She hadn’t seen it herself but heard about it from Kai... She seemed to be hiding when that thing passed over.
She couldn’t help but feel curious about it.
’Do they know where it is by now?’
[ Eliza: Hunt humans? What else would it do? The A.I. doesn’t waste resources unless it’s targeting something. ]
[ Joseph: Maybe it’s after Augmented Humans’ shelters. Strong humans attract danger. The machines always go for the biggest threats first. ]
[ Claire: So you’re saying being strong makes us a target? Great. ]
The chat buzzed with unease.
[ Renji: I read from a previous chat that the Origin Region has shelters full of Augmented Humans. If that fortress is heading west, maybe it’s going for them. ]
[ Connie: Augmented shelters aren’t safe. The stronger you are, the faster the A.I. notices you. ]
[ Tomas: But without Augmented Humans, how do we fight back? Weak shelters get wiped out anyway. ]
Mei also enjoyed these simple conversations.
Still, she decided to enter the shelter again as she noticed that the sky was already turning dark. There might be a storm coming...
Unfortunately, as soon as she heard the alarm, she knew that what was coming was even worse.

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Taking the UFO
paragraphs: A few moments ago, Mei pressed her body against the rubble as her Living Camouflage wrapped her in invisibility.
As soon as her Talent was triggered, the battlefield noise was muffled, her heat signature erased, and her movements were suppressed by Silent Veins Lv3.
She was like a phantom, unseen even by the advanced sensors of the Dragoons.
At this time, Desmond was already safe inside the main building, so she no longer had to worry about him.
Knowing that her dog had taken cover, it gave her freedom to act.
"I’m ready..." Mei muttered as she carried her Plasma Rifle that was warm in her hands. Since it was turned on, its charge indicator was glowing faintly.
She could already fire it at any time she wanted.
Of course, she had only one target in mind, the massive vessel hovering beyond the smoke.
It was unmistakable.
It had twin rotors that were stabilizing its wide, angular body...
She also noticed that it had gun mounts lined its sides, and beneath its belly, hatches were present, and it could probably be used for deploying more Sentinels.
Mei recognized it instantly... it looked almost identical to the Samson she had seen in the old film Avatar.
It was basically a transport and gunship hybrid, designed to dominate both air and ground.
As she got into position, her finger hovered near the trigger.
One shot to the rotors, maybe two, and she could cripple it.
The risk was enormous... Her camouflage would drop the moment she fired and failed to destroy it, she’d get into trouble. But if she didn’t act, the shelter could be obliterated.
Then Kai arrived.
She saw him below and seemed to have given Atom another Plasma Rifle with a charge. He seemed to be using the Chameleon Cloak he bought from the Gene Trader, making him so difficult to detect.
Nonetheless, with the two working together, they destroyed the last two Dragoons!
"Whoa!"
"Just one more! That large vessel!"
The defenders cheered weakly, but Kai ignored the celebration. Mei then saw Atom ditching the Plasma Rifle and taking out another weapon!
"Everyone, pull back! That UFO is charging up!" Kai shouted.
Mei’s eyes turned back to the vessel.
’UFO? Are we in Alien Invasion?’ As she thought of this, she saw that a hatch had opened, revealing a cannon glowing with energy!
The hum grew louder as the weapon started gathering power for a devastating strike!
But Kai didn’t fire at it. He didn’t even raise his weapon!
’What?’
Mei frowned. If he wouldn’t act, then she would. She steadied her aim, ready to break her concealment.
"Wait, Mei!"
The voice froze her.
Kai had sensed her. Somehow, even through her concealment, his skills pierced her stealth...
His eyes were actually locked on her position, though she was invisible to everyone else.
She hesitated, stunned at the sudden call.
Then she noticed Atom. The A‐Grade Sentinel that had switched weapons.
It was now carrying a heavy rifle designed to fire solid blocks of metal.
BOOM!
The weapon fired and a block of steel shot out like a cannonball, slamming into the vessel’s hull.
BOOM!
The impact shook the air. The gunship lost its balance as the cannon’s energy dissipated!
Somehow, the shelter was spared.
Mei lowered her rifle as she looked at Atom. Then, her eyes widened as realization struck. "Wait... Kai! Are you thinking of capturing that thing?!"
Kai grinned...
He was confident that he’d succeed.
Seeing Kai’s reaction, Mei knew she was right.
No wonder he hadn’t wanted her to fire.
Atom fired again, another block of metal smashing into the vessel’s side.
The gunship started failing with its rotors straining to keep balance.
Soon, she saw sparks break out from its weapon mount, the cannon was definitely damaged!
Kai then used his Keen Sense to the limit as he found the time...
"Suppress the rotors, Atom!" Kai commanded.

The Sentinel obeyed, firing two more blocks of metal. One struck the left rotor assembly, bending its frame. The other slammed into the underside hatch, jamming it shut before more Sentinels could deploy!
Boom! Boom!
The vessel wobbled and its flight path was destabilized. It wasn’t destroyed, but it was forced lower, closer to the ground.
Kai raised his hand, activating Spirit Pulse Lv5.
Suddenly! Energy surged outward, and a shockwave of Spirit power followed!
It was so strong that it rattled the vessel’s systems. The cannon’s charge finally stopped.
Mei watched in awe. "He’s disabling it... not destroying it. It might be possible to capture this thing..."
It didn’t end there...
Kai’s body blurred as he used Specter Step Lv3, vanishing from sight and reappearing closer to the vessel that had already lowered due to their constant attacks!
Furthermore, its mounted gun couldn’t lock on to him. Kai’s movement was ghostlike, unpredictable, and impossible to track thanks to his Cloak and Gene Skill!
"Go Atom! Put it down!" Kai shouted.
Just like that, Atom continued its barrage, firing block after block!
If the magazine was emptied, Atom would just put more in!
Each impact forced the vessel lower until its landing struts scraped the dirt!
However, it wasn’t done yet! The rotors screamed as it was trying to keep it airborne.
"Almost there!"
Kai leapt as he saw the vessel struggling...
Relying on his Bronze Skin Lv2 to harden and stabilize his body against the shockwave of rotor wash, he landed atop the vessel, and his hand pressed against its hull!
Bam!
"Fast Appraisal..." he muttered.
Data flooded his mind...
Now that it was level 5, various details came into his mind that wouldn’t be possible if not for his current level.
Soon, he even noticed the structural weaknesses, energy flow, weapon systems. He saw the vessel’s vulnerabilities as if they were highlighted in red!
It wasn’t just a notification from the system and a simple description anymore!
"There," he whispered, before activating Spirit Pulse into the highlighted node.
’Ok... No more Spirit Points...’
Thankfully, his move slowed the rotors, and the entire craft tilted before settling heavily onto the ground.
Crash!
Mei finally dropped her camouflage, stepping out of the haze with her rifle lowered. "You... you actually captured it."

chapters.title: Chapter 178: The Aerial Gunship
paragraphs: Kai smiled as soon as he managed to drop the flying vessel.
He couldn’t help but glance at the Appraisal Result once again.
[ You have discovered Aerial Gunship: "Impulse" ]
[ Grade: Advanced War Machine ]
[ Status: Incapacitated ]
[ Description: A twin‐rotor aerial gunship designed for both transport and heavy assault. Equipped with a machine gun, side‐mounted plasma cannons, and deployment hatches. ]
[ Note: Current condition is disabled due to rotor damage and system overload. ]
’So our UFO is called Impulse...’ Kai thought.
It was definitely a vessel that Kai wanted to have for himself!
At this time, Mei finally dropped her camouflage, stepping out of the haze with her rifle leaning on her shoulder.
"You... you actually captured it."
Kai exhaled... His body was trembling slightly from exhaustion. His Spirit Points were gone, drained by the repeated use of Spirit Pulse and Specter Step. He could no longer rely on his Gene Skills.
But he recalled something and studied the vessel. "It’s not over. There are still Sentinels inside."
Mei stiffened. "Inside?"
Kai nodded grimly. "The hatches were sealed when Atom hit them, but that doesn’t mean the cargo is empty. They’ll try to break out."
As if on cue, the vessel shuddered.
Then, Metallic thuds echoed from within, followed by the grinding of gears...
The captured Aerial Gunship seemed as if it were alive.
Kai turned to look behind and raised his voice.
"Atom! Delay them a bit! Don’t let them breach the shelter walls! We need to change the energy cells quick..."
The A‐Grade Sentinel obeyed instantly.
Its heavy rifle clanked as it reloaded another block of metal.
With a swift movement, Atom positioned itself near the vessel’s underside, where the hatches strained against their bent frames.
It didn’t take that long before he started dealing with the Sentinels.
BOOM!
The first block smashed into the hatch, denting it further and forcing the mechanism to jam. Sparks flew as the internal gears tried to force it open.
BOOM!
Another shot followed... This time, it was angled to ricochet inside the half‐open hatch! The impact reverberated through the vessel, and it immediately silenced the grinding noise.
Mei covered Kai’s flank with her Plasma Rifle as Kai changed his Energy Cell...
"If they break through, we’ll be ready."
Kai nodded. "Or maybe Atom can already deal with this... As you can see, if we fire plasma inside, we can risk destroying the vessel’s systems. I really want it intact."
"Ahhh... You’re right." Mei agreed as she saw the gunship tremble again.
A panel on its side buckled outward, and a Sentinel arm clawed through the gap.
Soon, its plasma weapon glowed faintly as it tried to pull itself free.
Atom reacted instantly! Dropping its heavy rifle, it charged forward.
Its gears whined as it grabbed the protruding arm and twisted.
Crash!
The Sentinel made them static noise before Atom ripped it clean off, and as its head popped out, Atom grabbed and crushed it before shoving the unit back inside.
CRASH!
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ +150 Experience Points ]
The hatch slammed shut again with sparks raining down.
Mei’s eyes widened. "Wow..."
Kai smiled, "Y-yeah... That’s impressive."
Inside the vessel, muffled impacts continued.
Soon, the hatch could no longer hold it, and it was thrown open!
At this time, Kai and the others were already with their Plasma Rifles, ready to deal with the remaining Sentinels...
However, Kai raised his hand as he didn’t want to fire at will with the gunship so close. At the very least, he wanted that as the last option if Atom failed to deal with the Sentinels.
Soon, four Sentinels spilled out, with their optics glowing red as a sign that they were in combat mode.
Once again, Kai’s hand shot up, reminding his team...
"Hold fire! Don’t damage the vessel!"
The defenders hesitated as they were also scared of the Sentinels, but they followed Kai... However, Atom didn’t.
The A‐Grade Sentinel charged forward, faster than the enemy units could react.
Its gears whined as it slammed into the first Sentinel, wrenching the plasma rifle from its grip!
It was a pity that the Rifle would no longer be usable, but it didn’t matter at this moment...
With a twist of its mechanical arms, Atom snapped the weapon in half and hurled the shards aside.
The second Sentinel fired, but Atom ducked low as it closed the distance.
It seized the barrel of the rifle, forcing the weapon upward.
Fwoosh~
The plasma bolt scorched the sky harmlessly before Atom tore the rifle free and smashed it across the unit’s head, sending sparks flying.
The third and fourth Sentinels tried to flank, but Atom turned sharply. It dropped the broken rifle and reached down, retrieving a blade from its own storage compartment!
It was a heavy combat knife forged for close‐quarters combat.
The blade glinted as Atom waved it!
CLANG!
The third Sentinel’s weapon was sliced clean in two... Then, Atom drove the blade into its chest, twisting until the unit collapsed in a heap of sparking wires.
The fourth Sentinel charged, swinging its rifle like a club!
Atom parried with the blade, as steel met alloy. With a swift counter, Atom slashed across its arm, severing the limb.
The disarmed unit backed off, before Atom plunged the blade into its core.
One by one, the four Sentinels fell with their bodies scattered across the dirt.
Soon, Atom stood over them, blade dripping with... oil.
Silence followed before the crowd cheered!
"Atom! Atom! Atom!"
"You’re the best!"
"Strongest Sentinel! Atom!"
Kai lowered his hand and finally relaxed.
He already confirmed with his Keen Senses that there were no more enemies inside the Impulse.
"It’s done. The vessel is ours."
Mei heaved a sigh of relief after hearing the confirmation.
"Captured... with minimal damage."
Unfortunately, two freed slaves lay motionless near the barricades... Their sacrifice was undeniable.
Kai bowed his head. "Two confirmed dead. They fought bravely."
Mei placed a hand on his shoulder. "We need to at least give them a proper burial..."
"That’s right." Kai agreed as he looked at the Aerial Gunship.
’You’re not empty, are you?’Kai thought as he recalled his Breathrough Requirements.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: Closer to Breakthrough
paragraphs: [ Breakthrough Requirement: To advance beyond Level 30, the Survivor must complete a special quest. ]
[ Quest: Strengthen your foundation.
Possess at least 5 Gene Skills upgraded to Level 5.
Absorb 10 B‐Grade Energy Cores.
Bind 3 Gene Weapons to your body. ]
[ Reward: Unlock Physique Evolution. Gain access to advanced stat growth and new Gene Skill compatibility. ]
[ Survivor will remain capped at Level 30 until the requirement is fulfilled. ]
After a short celebration, Kai wasted no time.
He turned to the weary defenders and gave instructions.
"Gather everything you can from the battlefield. Strip the Dragoons, collect the Sentinel parts, and don’t leave a single item behind. Every piece matters."
The freed workers nodded... They were still trying to compose themselves after seeing their dead companions but they moved quickly.
Soon, they dragged the wreckage toward the shelter, stacking broken rifles, scorched metals, and shattered circuits...
Even the drained cores from fallen Sentinels were carefully pried out and placed into crates.
Kai’s eyes then shifted back to Atom.
The A‐Grade Sentinel had already begun moving toward the Impulse with its sensors scanning the hull.
He knew that look... Atom was preparing to enter.
"Atom! Stop!" Kai shouted
Atom froze from where it stood with its optics’ lights dissipating.
Kai strode forward, his tone firm. "Not this time. Stay away from the vessel."
Mei tilted her head. "Why? Atom could clear it faster."

Kai shook his head. "No. Atom doesn’t distinguish between salvage and prize. It would absorb whatever it finds... energy sources, rare alloys, maybe even the control systems themselves. If that happens, the Impulse will be useless to us. This loot belongs to me."
Indeed, Kai had seen it for several times already. This time, Kai couldn’t allow that to happen.
Furthermore, he wanted to repair this Aerial Gunship...
If Atom absorbed something from it and they had no idea what it was and couldn’t replace it, then this vessel would become useless.
Thankfully, Atom paused, then stepped back obediently. Its blade retracted into storage, and it resumed a silent guard stance beside the vessel.
Kai exhaled, relieved. "Good. Now it’s my turn."
He climbed into the Impulse, forcing open the cockpit hatch.
The interior was dim, lit only by the faint glow of emergency systems. The smell of scorched circuits and burnt oil filled the air...
It needed lots of repair for sure, but it shouldn’t be impossible to fix.
Anyway, the cockpit was cramped but functional. Twin pilot seats faced a wide array of controls, most of them cracked or sparking.
Transparent displays also appeared with unreadable data, while the overhead canopy was simply an armored glass.
Kai ran his hand across the console. "This thing... I don’t think A.I. Aria built this... Must be the Anima Civilization."

He then moved deeper, past the cockpit into the storage bay. The walls were lined with racks for Sentinel deployment, though most were empty now. At the corner, he found a metallic briefcase, probably thrown away during the chaos.
Then, at the center, there was a containment unit and Kai believed that the core was there.
For now, Kai checked the metallic briefcase.
Kai pried it open quite easily, and his eyes went wide...
"Twenty?"
Inside were twenty crystalline cores, each pulsing faintly with energy. He immediately triggered Fast Appraisal skill...
[ You have discovered B‐Grade Energy Core! ]
[ Description: A condensed energy source harvested from advanced war machines. Provides immense Spirit energy when absorbed. ]
[ Requirement: Can only be absorbed by Survivors with a Physique Rating of C- or higher. ]
[ Effect: Upon absorption, the Energy Core will permanently enhance the host’s body, unlocking the potential to surpass human limits and receive a chance to break through the Level 30 bottleneck. ]
[ Warning: Absorption is irreversible. Failure to meet requirements may result in fatal overload. ]
"What the..."
Kai counted carefully...
"There are really twenty of them. Now I’m only lacking Skill Points and decent Gene Weapons."

Well, he needed five Gene Skills reaching Level 5, but getting a Skill Point alone was not easy. Because of that, he would have to rely on his Trailblazer Title, which helps with the mastery increase and his Skill Usage to level it up without Skill Points.
As for the Gene Weapons... He already had one that was a Low-Grade.
Needless to say, he hadn’t bound one of them yet since, according to Sera and Althea, there was no way of unbinding it.
He didn’t want to get stuck with a Low-Grade Gene Weapon right now.
Unless he was desperate, he’d not consider binding one yet.
In the meantime, with Kai’s orders, the survivors worked tirelessly through the afternoon.

Atom coordinated the heavy lifting, as it helped drag the massive Impulse Gunship across the battlefield. The freed workers, though exhausted and grieving, pushed themselves to assist. Chains, pulleys, and improvised sleds were rigged together, and slowly, inch by inch, the captured vessel was hauled inside the shelter walls.
The barricades had been battered, but Kai refused to leave them broken.
"Rebuild the wall," he commanded. "We can’t afford another breach."
By dusk, scorched planks were replaced, gaps filled with salvaged metal sheets, and the perimeter looked a little decent now.
The shelter looked scarred, but it was alright.
The Impulse was now inside the compound near the crop fields...
Finally, Freedom Shelter had an aerial war machine under its control.
That night, Kai was already considering building a Guild... He already has enough Survivor Medals anyway... He was hoping that he’d actually get a reward like Skill Points from it.
In any case, he lay on his bed, staring at the ceiling, replaying the previous battle in his head.
’I could’ve ended it faster if I targeted well.’He mused.
Then, as he was about to fall asleep, a knock came at his door.
Kai sat up, confused. "Who is it?"
The door creaked open, and Mei stepped inside.
She had already bathed, her hair was damp and loose with fresh new clothes.
The scent of soap lingered faintly, and Kai couldn’t help but take a deep breath.
"Kai," she said softly while closing the door behind her.
"Mei? It’s late."

chapters.title: Chapter 180: B-Grade Core
paragraphs: Kai sat up straighter as Mei closed the door behind her.
The faint scent of soap lingered in the air. She was definitely clean compared to the smoke and oil that had clung to them all day.
Mei didn’t waste time. "Kai... those cores you found. What are they for?"
’Ohhh... So you’re for that?’
Kai immediately composed himself before he replied.

"Just like that C-Grade Cores you absorbed to break through Level 5, they’re the same items. But this time, only Survivors at Level 30 can use them. If you reach that level, I’ll share them with you. Until then, they’re useless and dangerous to anyone else."
Someone might try absorbing them without a sufficient level, so he decided to store it in his limited Inventory Slots.
Mei nodded slowly as she already guessed this far. Still, hearing Kai’s confirmation made her happy.
"So they’re not just for you. You’d let me use them too?"
Kai gave a faint smile. "Of course. We survive together. If you reach Level 30, I’ll make sure you have what you need."
She hesitated, then shifted the topic.
"What about Atom? Could I use its abilities to explore ruins?"
"Mhmm?" Kai paused at the sudden change of topic.
Mei also noticed this and quickly explained.
"As you know, before I saw you and your shelter, I traveled a lot. I found several shelters... some were decent, but one of them..." Her voice hardened as she recalled it...
"One was run by a nasty Survivor. His talent allowed him to produce clean water, so he controlled everything. People had no choice but to obey him."
Kai was stunned to hear this and nodded.
It was no wonder Mei was concerned about it. Back on Earth, she would always take care of her officemates, old or new, in her own way. It was quite normal for her to feel this...

"I understand your concern. But Atom may not be able to handle long expeditions right now. Its battery isn’t infinite. I can’t see its exact energy level, but I know combat drains it heavily. And since I prohibited Atom from absorbing anything from the Impulse, its reserves are lower than usual."
Mei frowned. "So it’s weaker now."
Kai nodded. "Yes. Still, once Atom completes its special recharge, I’ll join you. We’ll explore together. I don’t plan to stay stuck in one shelter forever."
Her eyes widened slightly. "You want to leave Freedom Shelter?"

Kai shook his head. "Not abandon it. Think of it like this... I want a home... a place to return to. That’s why I’ll reinforce Freedom and Haven‐45 first. But eventually, I’ll explore the larger human city marked on the map. That’s where the real answers are."
Mei studied him for a long moment, then smiled faintly. "You always think ahead. That’s why people follow you."
Kai chuckled softly. "And that’s why I need people like you beside me."
The silence stretched, but it wasn’t uncomfortable. Mei moved closer, sitting on the edge of his bed.
Her damp hair brushed his shoulder, and Kai felt the warmth of her presence.
"You should rest," she whispered.
Kai met her gaze, and for a moment, none of them spoke.
The tension of the day, the relief of survival, and the unspoken bond between them hung in the air.
Slowly, they leaned closer.
The night passed quietly...
When morning came, the weather seemed to be a lot better
Kai stirred awake, and soon, his mind was already shifting back to plans and requirements he must complete...
At this time, Mei was already gone, but the faint scent of her still lingered in the room.
Outside, Mei stepped into the corridor, her hair tied back, as she planned to go straight to the mess hall...
At this time, however, Claire, carrying a basket of supplies, stopped mid‐step. Her eyes widened as she saw Mei leaving Kai’s room.
Mei froze for a moment, then offered a small nod. "Morning."
Claire then smiled at her but said nothing.
She simply watched as Mei walked away... Soon, her figure disappeared down the hall.
At this time, Kai sat alone in his room.
He wasn’t in a hurry to go out since the shelter was not in danger, and he could just get food anytime he wanted.
First, he confirmed that his Spirit Points had already recovered... It was a good thing since it affects his body to some degree as well.
With that in mind, he opened his inventory and pulled out the metallic briefcase.
The faint glow of twenty crystalline cores was beautiful.
"Time to test it."
He then reached in, carefully selecting one of the cores.
Its surface was cool to the touch, unlike the C-Grade Core that was quite warm.
For now. He closed the briefcase and stored it back into his inventory, leaving only the single core in his hand.
The moment he pressed it against his chest, the system responded and confirmed the absorption process!
The process didn’t take that long, and he soon received a familiar message. This time, it truly was a lot better than a C-grade!
[ Energy Core absorption complete. ]
[ Health Points +20 ]
[ Spirit Points +5 ]
[ Physique Rating has slightly improved. ]
[ Proficiency of all Gene Skills has slightly increased. ]
[ You have received Skill Points +1 ]
Kai’s eyes widened as the surge of energy coursed through him. The 20 Health Points and 5 Spirit Points weren’t something he could ignore.
Furthermore, even if his Physique was already Grade C, he could still feel any slight improvement because of his Keen Sense.
He flexed his hand, feeling the subtle increase in resilience, and gently nodded.
"Pretty neat for a single core..." Kai muttered.
Nonetheless, what truly caught his attention was the notification at the end.
"A Skill Point..." Kai muttered with a green. "That’s exactly what I needed."
He knew very well how difficult it was to get Skill Points.
Since B-Grades could give him one, he had to abuse this for sure.
However, as he was about to continue absorbing more, he heard the sound of vehicles’ engines rumbling outside the shelter!

Kai gave a faint smile.
"Of course.
We survive together.
If you reach Level 30, I’ll make sure you have what you need."
She hesitated, then shifted the topic.
"What about Atom?
Could I use its abilities to explore ruins?"
"Mhmm?" Kai paused at the sudden change of topic.
Mei also noticed this and quickly explained.
"As you know, before I saw you and your shelter, I traveled a lot.
I found several shelters... some were decent, but one of them..." Her voice hardened as she recalled it...
"One was run by a nasty Survivor.
His talent allowed him to produce clean water, so he controlled everything.
People had no choice but to obey him."
Kai was stunned to hear this and nodded.
It was no wonder Mei was concerned about it.
Back on Earth, she would always take care of her officemates, old or new, in her own way.
It was quite normal for her to feel this...
"I understand your concern.
But Atom may not be able to handle long expeditions right now.
Its battery isn’t infinite.
I can’t see its exact energy level, but I know combat drains it heavily.
And since I prohibited Atom from absorbing anything from the Impulse, its reserves are lower than usual."
Mei frowned.
"So it’s weaker now."
Kai nodded.
"Yes.
Still, once Atom completes its special recharge, I’ll join you.
We’ll explore together.
I don’t plan to stay stuck in one shelter forever."
Her eyes widened slightly.
"You want to leave Freedom Shelter?"
Kai shook his head.
"Not abandon it.
Think of it like this...
I want a home... a place to return to.
That’s why I’ll reinforce Freedom and Haven‐45 first.
But eventually, I’ll explore the larger human city marked on the map.
That’s where the real answers are."
Mei studied him for a long moment, then smiled faintly.
"You always think ahead.
That’s why people follow you."
Kai chuckled softly.
"And that’s why I need people like you beside me."
The silence stretched, but it wasn’t uncomfortable.
Mei moved closer, sitting on the edge of his bed.
Her damp hair brushed his shoulder, and Kai felt the warmth of her presence.
"You should rest," she whispered.
Kai met her gaze, and for a moment, none of them spoke.
The tension of the day, the relief of survival, and the unspoken bond between them hung in the air.
Slowly, they leaned closer.
The night passed quietly...
When morning came, the weather seemed to be a lot better
Kai stirred awake, and soon, his mind was already shifting back to plans and requirements he must complete...
At this time, Mei was already gone, but the faint scent of her still lingered in the room.
Outside, Mei stepped into the corridor, her hair tied back, as she planned to go straight to the mess hall...
At this time, however, Claire, carrying a basket of supplies, stopped mid‐step.
Her eyes widened as she saw Mei leaving Kai’s room.
Mei froze for a moment, then offered a small nod.
"Morning."
Claire then smiled at her but said nothing.
She simply watched as Mei walked away...
Soon, her figure disappeared down the hall.
At this time, Kai sat alone in his room.
He wasn’t in a hurry to go out since the shelter was not in danger, and he could just get food anytime he wanted.
First, he confirmed that his Spirit Points had already recovered...
It was a good thing since it affects his body to some degree as well.
With that in mind, he opened his inventory and pulled out the metallic briefcase.
The faint glow of twenty crystalline cores was beautiful.
"Time to test it."
He then reached in, carefully selecting one of the cores.
Its surface was cool to the touch, unlike the C-Grade Core that was quite warm.
For now.
He closed the briefcase and stored it back into his inventory, leaving only the single core in his hand.
The moment he pressed it against his chest, the system responded and confirmed the absorption process!
The process didn’t take that long, and he soon received a familiar message.
This time, it truly was a lot better than a C-grade!
[ Energy Core absorption complete. ]
[ Health Points +20 ]
[ Spirit Points +5 ]
[ Physique Rating has slightly improved. ]
[ Proficiency of all Gene Skills has slightly increased. ]
[ You have received Skill Points +1 ]
Kai’s eyes widened as the surge of energy coursed through him.
The 20 Health Points and 5 Spirit Points weren’t something he could ignore.
Furthermore, even if his Physique was already Grade C, he could still feel any slight improvement because of his Keen Sense.
He flexed his hand, feeling the subtle increase in resilience, and gently nodded.
"Pretty neat for a single core..." Kai muttered.
Nonetheless, what truly caught his attention was the notification at the end.
"A Skill Point..." Kai muttered with a green.
"That’s exactly what I needed."
He knew very well how difficult it was to get Skill Points.
Since B-Grades could give him one, he had to abuse this for sure.
However, as he was about to continue absorbing more, he heard the sound of vehicles’ engines rumbling outside the shelter!

chapters.title: Chapter 181: Threat
paragraphs: The rumble of engines grew louder, echoing across the fields outside Freedom Shelter.
Unlike the deeper sound of his Armored Vehicle, this sound was sharper and faster... Without a doubt, they were motorbikes.
At this time, dust clouds rose as nine riders approached their shelter.
Their headlights could be easily recognized in the early morning haze. They moved in formation, circling once before halting just beyond the rebuilt barricades.
These weren’t strangers to the area.
For weeks, they had been observing the A.I. base from a distance, waiting for the right moment. They had seen the Dragoons and some Sentinels patrol the area...
They had even encountered some D-Grade Sentinels before that led them to discover this place.
But now, the machines guarding this area were gone. Humans had taken over and it disrupted their plans.
Needless to say, they couldn’t just ignore what had happened. Today, they decided to make their move.
The leader dismounted first.
He was tall, broad‐shouldered, with a scar running across his cheek. His rifle wasn’t ordinary. It was a Plasma Rifle that rested in his grip. The others carried standard rifles, worn but functional.

He raised his voice, introducing himself. "Name’s Angelo. We were from Shelter‐28... At least before it was destroyed during the mech siege event. Now, let’s just say we’re Survivors in the ruins of a nearby town. We’re here to say hello..."
There was no way they were only here to greet them... Nonetheless, eight bikers stood behind him, and they were just watching the situation unfold.
They also looked a little nervous, but their leader seemed so confident that they wouldn’t just get peppered with bullets by the guards standing on the wooden ramparts...
Soon, Kai appeared and observed the group.

Their gear was mismatched. They weren’t the Survivor Gear issued by the system. Still, they seemed better even if they were just scavenged armor plates, patched jackets, and helmets with cracked visors.
They looked like men who had fought too many battles and lost too many homes.
Kai stood atop the ramparts as he studied them.
Their set of equipment was functional but crude...
Still, they were armed, disciplined, and clearly experienced.
He called down and started questioning them. In this apocalypse, where resources were extremely important, he couldn’t just trust anyone.
"What’s your reason for coming here?"
Angelo adjusted his grip on the Plasma Rifle.
"Trade. We’re short on food and daily necessities. We can last a month or two with what we have, but it’ll run out quickly. We thought maybe you would be willing to deal with us."
Kai was impressed with his honesty, but it was definitely not everything... Well, he knew desperation when he heard it.

Angelo continued, explaining that even with their ability to plant crops, it would take several months before they could take advantage of it. He also continued explaining that their water was limited. He wanted to continue emphasizing the fact that their shelter had a few extra motorbikes and they wanted to use them to conduct some simple trade, until his eyes shifted.
’What?’
He noticed the woman beside Kai, standing tall with her rifle slung across her shoulder.
Needless to say, it was Mei.
For a moment, Angelo froze.

His eyes widened slightly, shock flashing across his face. Their current shelter lacked women entirely. The sight of Mei, a young, beautiful, confident, and clearly clean as if she’d just taken a bath... stirred something in him.
Excitement, curiosity, perhaps even greed.
But Angelo corrected his expression immediately, forcing his features back into neutrality.
"Ahem... Where was I?"
He cleared his throat, pretending nothing had happened.
Kai caught the change in Angelo’s eyes. Of course, he didn’t miss details, and he didn’t like the way Angelo looked at Mei.
Nonetheless, Angelo finished his piece, and the bikers waited for Kai’s response.
Kai sighed as he could tell that motorbikes could be more useful than their set of bikes.
However, he wasn’t really that desperate to have motorbikes.
"So you’re only trading motorbikes? No fuel?" He asked.
Angelo smirked faintly. "Fuel’s tricky, I’ll admit. But depending on what you’re willing to trade, we might be able to arrange something. Still, our priority right now is food. How about it?"

Kai gently nodded. Even their own armored vehicles were rarely used, the shelter had only a few gallons left, and every trip had to be carefully used. It was the same for the motorbikes. Without fuel were little more than scrap metal.
"How about MREs? I think we still have some extras..." Kai said.
Angelo’s eyes lit up. "Now that’s something we can work with." He stepped forward...
"Right... If you’re willing to trade, I’ll invite you to our place. The shelter we occupy might have more things you’d find useful."

He paused, then added... "The town we settled in was hidden by a thick fog. Most people wouldn’t have found it, but one of our survivors had a Talent that made us discover it. Thanks to him, we discovered a lot of intact structures. A dealership filled with motorbikes... and even a fuel truck."
Kai nodded. It was no wonder they’re on their motorbikes roaming the area...

Of course, there was no way they’d reveal everything to strangers. It just meant Angelo’s group had access to something far more valuable than they were admitting, that they didn’t mind revealing some of their cards.
Angelo spread his hands, trying to look open and honest. "We’re not asking for charity. We’ve got things to offer. But food... food is what we need most."
As he spoke, his gaze turned toward Mei again.
Angelo’s eyes lingered just a fraction too long. It seemed that a shelter with no women was starting to get unbearable for him.
"Ahem... as I said, we’re here to trade." Angelo said as he shifted his gaze.
Kai frowned and shook his head... He didn’t like it.

"Now that I think about it... Food is our lifeline too. We can’t afford to trade it away, not for motorbikes or fuel. Even if your ruins have other things we might find useful, we don’t have enough food to spare."
The bikers shifted uneasily, exchanging glances.
At this time, Angelo’s smirk faded, replaced by a colder expression. He tilted his Plasma Rifle slightly, not in threat, but as if to remind everyone that he wasn’t powerless.

"I see... You’re turning us away. That’s your choice. But remember... supplies don’t stay hidden forever. If you won’t share, someone else will come to take them. And when that day comes, don’t expect mercy."
Kai stared coldly at Angelo and asked...
"Is that a threat?"

chapters.title: Chapter 182: The New Event and the Start of the First Organization
paragraphs: Angelo gave a short laugh, though his eyes stayed cold.

Even if Kai’s group now knew that his shelter had spare motorbikes and fuel tanks, it didn’t matter. After all, Angelo’s side had already learned something just as important... the shelter in front of them had MREs inside.

"Call it whatever you want. Threat, warning... doesn’t matter. Just remember, we’ve survived worse than this. If you think you can keep everything locked away, sooner or later someone will come knocking harder than we did today. It’s not too late to trade with us..."
Kai didn’t flinch. "Then let them try." He had no reason to waste more words.

Although Kai had no idea what kind of Talents or Gene Skills these bikers possessed, it didn’t matter. Angelo’s group was also unaware of Freedom Shelter’s true capabilities. That balance of uncertainty kept both sides cautious.

For a moment, the two men stared at each other across the barricades. The bikers behind Angelo shifted nervously, gripping their rifles. The guards on the ramparts tightened their hold on their weapons, waiting for Kai’s signal.
Finally, Angelo swung his leg over his motorbike.

’They must be recuperating. There’s no way they occupied this shelter without casualties... However, there are only nine of us right now. It would be better to call for backup and return at night,’Angelo mused. He didn’t dare underestimate their force.
He wasn’t arrogant enough to believe his Talent and Skills alone would be enough to raid this place.
Still, he was hoping to lure some of them outside and ambush them to make things easier. But that tactic was useless if they refused to leave the shelter.

"Fine. We’ll leave. But our offer is still open. In case you change your mind, you’ll find us in a swamp in this direction. Once we notice your arrival, we’ll lift the fog to let you in." Angelo kept his tone calm. He didn’t want them to grow too suspicious about his shelter.
Soon, the engines roared to life. Just like that, dust rose as the nine bikers finally left.
Mei then stepped closer to Kai. "Are you sure? They’ll be back..."
Kai nodded. "It’s fine... Let’s prepare for now. Even if they have plans, I don’t think they’ll be able to act freely."
The guards relaxed slightly, but the tension was still there...
Everyone inside Freedom Shelter understood what Angelo’s words meant. The bikers were desperate, and desperate men were dangerous.
However, it seemed that Kai was already aware of what was about to happen...
Apparently, a few hours later, a system message appeared.
It was another Global Event!
This time, it was no longer a Mech Siege Event or a Field Boss Event. It was something completely different.
[ Global Event is Here! ]
[ Upcoming Hostile Operation: Surveillance Sweep ]
[ Countdown: 5 Days ]
[ Duration: 7 Days ]

[ Objective: Survive continuous drone sweeps across all regions. Drones will scan for survivors, marking detected targets for hunter bot deployment. Survivors must hide, jam signals, or destroy drones or face the reinforcements of the Swarmers. ]
[ Rewards: High Experience Points, Rare Loot Drops, Survivor’s Medal, Signal Jamming Devices, and others ]

[ Additional Notice: Surveillance Drones operate in waves, covering wide areas. Once a survivor is marked, hunter bots will arrive within minutes. Shelters are advised to minimize outdoor activity and prepare countermeasures. ]
[ Estimated Enemy Composition: Swarmer, Hounds, Hunters, and a special one. ]
"Another event!"
"This time... It’s about the surveillance drones."
"This is going to be tricky. I think we need to hide underground."
"But we have Signal Jammers."
"R-right... I think Kai can produce them."
They all had mixed reactions.
For now, Kai just read the glowing message carefully.
"Five days until it begins... and it lasts for a full week. This is very straightforward. Drones will sweep from the skies and lands, marking survivors. If they tag us, hunters will follow."
"Hunters, huh... I’ve never seen them before. Kai, how about you?" Claire said.
"Me neither," Kai replied.
"I think surviving underground isn’t an issue... But what about those Hounds?" Mei muttered as she recalled those dog robots.
"Yeah... We have to either eliminate them while our jammer is active or just hide from them completely." Kai replied.
"At least, it’s only for seven days. We can’t move freely for that duration, but that should be fine." Claire added.
Although even simple trips outside could get them detected, it wasn’t really a big deal, considering Kai’s talent.
"But what do you think this special one noted at the end?" Claire asked as she looked at the Estimated Enemy Composition...
"Well, it’s probably the A.I. Army’s robot that can detect even if you hide underground or something... If not that, maybe a strong enemy that will come to us once we’re detected." Kai replied.
"Mhmm... Makes sense. It’s probably a unit that can bypass our jammer or something." Mei added.
"Alright... let’s prepare for this event. Just forget about that Angelo. They’ll be busy as well." Kai muttered.
Soon, Kai walked toward the warehouse... Inside, the shelves were stacked with supplies, but it was not enough.
He was here for an obvious reason. He needed to restock since they would be hiding from the Swarmers and Hounds...
Just like that, he activated his Talent and to take out an enhanced version of the Stealth Gift Pack.
[ Stealth Gift Pack (Enhanced) Contents: ghillie suit, enhanced night vision goggles, smoke grenade, stun grenade, and signal jammer ]
"I need more signal jammer..." Kai muttered as he began stockpiling them.
Next, Kai claimed dozens of Food Gift Packs (Enhanced).
Finally, Kai summoned the Energy Gift Pack (Enhanced).
Freedom Shelter relied on solar energy, but Kai knew they couldn’t risk using panels during the event. The heat and light could give away their position.
Instead, they would depend on battery‐powered devices for light and communication.
After finishing all of this, Kai finally made up his mind.
"Surveillance Sweep, huh..." Kai muttered.
"I guess I need to build a Guild now."
Without any hesitation, he opened his System and selected the Guild Feature...
[ Do you want to join or create a Guild? ]

chapters.title: Chapter 183: The Guild
paragraphs: Kai remembered to check his Survivor Medals...
Seeing that he still had 21 of them, he turned back his attention to the glowing prompt.
[ Do you want to join or create a Guild? ]
He already knew the answer.
With the upcoming Global Event, he knew that they needed a more organized structure and perhaps, even a method to grow stronger before this Surveillance Sweep started.
Kai tapped [ Create ].
Another window appeared.
[ 10 Survivor Medals have been deducted from your Inventory. ]
[ Guild Creation Form ]
[ Please enter Guild Name. ]
[ Please select Guild Banner. ]
[ Please confirm Guild Motto. ]
"Wow... Just like those games in the past..."
Kai exhaled slowly as he considered what to name.
"Guild name... huh." He muttered to himself, staring at the empty text box.

To be honest, he already thought of a few names ever since he learned about the Guild System. Names like Hidden Leaf, Phyrexia, Primarchs, Blank, Adventurers, and a few others had come into his mind. However, he was still undecided.
He knew the Guild Name would carry their legacy. It couldn’t be chosen carelessly, and he refused to half‐ass it.
Though he liked the sound of the Adventurers Guild as it would probably attract many Survivors, he still felt that it was not appropriate.
For now, he thought about their enemy... the A.I. Army. Machines scanning the skies, swarming the ground, hunting survivors like prey.
"We’re fighting against rebels made of steel. The name should reflect some kind of defiance against these machines... Hmm."
His mind drifted to Mei.
At night, when she visited him, she often confided her fears.
Well, she wasn’t a soldier or a fighter. She was just an office worker before the apocalypse. She admitted more than once that she wanted to go home, back to a life that no longer existed.
But there was nothing he could do but to comfort her.
’That’s obvious...’
Kai sighed as he was well aware that many Survivors really wanted to return to Earth and return to their normal lives without the threat of human-hunting machines.
Kai clenched his fist.
He recalled Mei’s voice... It was trembling yet honest, which stayed with him.
She was afraid, but she still stood beside him. The Guild name couldn’t just be a symbol of defiance against machines... it had to be a promise.
Kai clenched his fist as he made up his mind.
"This should be it..."
He typed slowly...
"Codebreakers"
It told the world exactly what they stood for... a Guild dedicated to dismantling the A.I. rebels, tearing apart their systems, and reclaiming the future.
It was both a declaration of war and a promise of return... to Earth.
Ding!
Just like that, the name was accepted.
Next, the banner selection appeared.
It looked like an online game interface, dozens of preset designs scrolling past his eyes.
Shields, swords, flames, animals. He paused at one design... a black banner with a silver gear emblem, crossed by a single spear.
The gear symbolized the enemy... the machines. The spear symbolized their will to fight back as it was piercing through their mechanical dominance.
He adjusted the color scheme and made a black background with a silver emblem and crimson highlights.
"Yeah... this works," Kai muttered.
Finally, the motto field appeared.
He didn’t think too much of it. It was probably for recruitment purposes...
Without hesitation, he typed... Human Will Triumph Over Machine.
He confirmed the creation.
System notifications flooded his vision.
[ Guild Created Successfully! ]
[ Guild Name: Corebreakers Guild ]
[ Guild Banner: Black with Silver Gear and Crimson Spear ]
[ Guild Motto: Human Will Triumph Over Machine ]
[ Guild Features Activated: Guild Chat, Guild Storage, Guild Missions, Guild Reputation ]
[ Guild Limit: 50 Members ]
[ Passive Buff: +5% Spirit Points recovery. ]
[ You have obtained 100 Reputation Points. ]
Kai nodded. "Five percent? Good. That’s exactly what we need."
But the notifications didn’t stop.
[ Announcement: The first Guild has been created! ]
[ Guild: Codebreakers Guild ]
[ Leader: Kai ]
[ This announcement has been broadcasted to World Chat. ]
Kai was stunned as he saw this notification.
"World Chat... so everyone knows now."
He imagined survivors across the continent seeing the message. Some would probably be curious, but he knew that some would be envious.
Then another notification appeared!
[ Congratulations! You are the First Guild Leader! ]
[ Special Rewards Granted: Talent Upgrade Crystal, Free Mission Pass ]
Kai’s eyes lit up... "Talent Upgrade Crystal again? I’m so lucky... and a Free Mission Pass?"
He already knew about the Talent Upgrade Crystal, and he was already excited to use it. However, the Free Mission Pass confused him.
[ Free Mission Pass: This pass can be used to instantly complete one Guild Mission without performing the requirements. ]
Kai smirked. "That’s... powerful."
He closed the window and leaned back against the warehouse wall. "So this is what it means to be the first Guild. The system rewards are quite generous..."
Kai couldn’t help but smile as he checked his Guild Window...
Soon, his attention turned to the Guild Mission Tab.
"Alright... Let’s see what kind of mission we have here..."
[ Guild Missions Available ]
He tapped it, and three prompts appeared in front of him.
[ Mission 1: Supply Run ]
Difficulty: Low
Objective: Submit 100 units of food to the Guild Storage within 48 hours.
Reward: Guild Reputation +50, Energy Core (C-Grade) x5 ]
"Oh? I can get cores here? This is nice...’Kai mused as he turned to the next stall.
[ Mission 2: Patrol Sweep ]
[ Difficulty: Low
Objective: Eliminate 10 roaming drones within the designated area.
Reward: Guild Reputation +75, Passive Buff +3% stamina recovery to all Clan Members for 24 hours. ]
[ Mission 3: Survivor Integration ]
[ Difficulty: Low
Objective: Recruit 15 survivors into the Guild.
Reward: Guild Reputation +10, Energy Core (C-Grade) x2 ]
Kai studied the list carefully. "So this is how Guild Missions work..."

Just as Kai was speculating about the Guild Mission, the warehouse door creaked open. Claire and Mei stepped inside... At this time, their expressions showed that they’d seen the World Chat announcement.
Claire then spoke first... "So, when are you going to invite me?"
"Ah... You saw the announcement?" Kai asked.
"Of course," Meil replied. "Everyone did. The whole continent knows you’re the first Guild Leader now. Don’t think you can keep me out. Is there a position within the Guild? I want one."

chapters.title: Chapter 184: The Features and the World’s Reaction
paragraphs: Kai was also curious and checked his notifications...
"Positions, huh... The system didn’t mention ranks yet. But I can probably assign roles once I get a member. For now, it’s just me as Leader."
Mei nodded and stepped forward. "I... I want to join too. Let me be the first member!"
Claire wryly smiled at this. She didn’t really care who got invited first, so she just let her be.
"I’m next then..."
She then paused as she recalled the chat...
"I wonder what’s going on in the World Chat right now. I’m sure they’re surprised. They probably didn’t even consider that there’s a Guild Feature in this Apocalypse."
The moment she noticed that there was an announcement, she immediately closed the World Chat and checked Kai in the warehouse after all.
Kai chuckled. "That notification definitely attracted everyone’s attention..."
Mei nodded as she felt that this was also a good thing. She just knew that it be advantageous to be part of a well-known guild.
Claire also added. "They’ll probably want to be part of the first guild. Right, what about the rewards? I’m sure you got some awesome things..."
Kai shrugged and explained the rewards he got.
"Yes... It includes Talent Upgrade Crystal and Free Mission Pass."
Mei’s eyes lit up..."That’s insane. You can upgrade your Talent again? T-that’s OP! Maybe your Weapons Gift Pack can give us a Laser Gun now or something."
"That’s awesome... But what’s the pass?" Claire asked.
"It just means we can skip one Guild Mission instantly. That could save us in a crisis. For now, there’s only Low-Grade Missions. If we have a High-Grade one, I’ll use the pass then." Kai explained.
Then, Kai finally sent the invitation.
[ Invitation Sent: Mei ]
[ Invitation Sent: Claire ]
System notifications chimed.
[ Mei has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Claire has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
Just as the invitations were confirmed, another set of notifications appeared before Kai’s eyes.
[ Congratulations! You have new Guild Members! ]
[ Guild Leader Notice ]
[ As Guild Leader, you may assign up to 3 Vice Leaders and 10 Elders. ]
[ Vice Leaders may: freely deposit and withdraw from Guild Storage, invite new members, manage Guild Reputation, edit Guild Motto, remove Guild Members, and assign or demote Elders. ]
[ Elders may: freely deposit and withdraw from Guild Storage, invite new members, manage Guild Reputation, and lead Guild Missions. ]
Kai rubbed his chin. "So Vice Leaders really are second‐in‐command... they even have the authority to kick members out. Elders are more like mission captains."
Of course, for ordinary members, being able to access some Guild Features like Chat, Missions, and even the Guild Buff was already incredible.
Claire heard this, and it seemed reasonable... "Sounds perfect for me. I’d be great at kicking people out if they’re not great... Will you make me a Vice Leader?"

Mei laughed nervously. "That’s... not something to be proud of. Anyway, I’m not good at managing people... But I don’t think that you’ll have many options for the Vice Leader position. You need people you can trust."
Kai smirked. "Don’t worry. I know I can trust the two of you. You can both hold the position. For now, let’s just focus on building the Guild."
Mei tilted her head curiously. "By the way... the motto. Did you write it yourself, or was it random?"
Kai chuckled. "I wrote it. Human Will Triumph Over Machine. It felt right."
Claire raised an eyebrow. "Hmmm... It sounds kinda serious and dramatic... but it makes sense."
Mei giggled. "I thought it was the system’s default. But if you wrote it... well, it does sound like you."
Kai shrugged. "It’s simple and direct actually... We’re fighting machines, so the motto should remind everyone what we stand for."
Claire pointed at the banner design on the interface. "And the banner? A gear with a spear? Even some red highlights... You really went for the edgy look, huh. I like it..."
"Edgy?" Kai was stunned as he also started questioning his decision.
However, to his eyes, it didn’t really look that bad.
Mei covered her mouth, laughing. "It’s not bad... She’s just teasing you..."

Kai rolled his eyes but smiled faintly. "Hey, it’s symbolic. The gear represents the machines, and the spear represents us piercing through them. Crimson is for blood or our sacrifice... It’s not about fashion."
Claire grinned. "Sure, sure. Keep telling yourself that. But don’t blame me if people think we’re some hardcore cult instead of a Guild."
Mei shook her head, still smiling. "No... I think it’s fine. It feels powerful. Survivors will take it seriously."
Just like that, the three laughed together, making the people outside curious about their conversation.
But as expected, the World Chat was already going crazy as soon as they realized that a Guild could actually be created!
Now, they have something to look forward to!

Many of them were already thinking of getting stronger with their fellow Survivors within their shelters to build their own Guild, while some others just wanted to focus on themselves and grow stronger to be invited by the best Guilds that would surely appear in the near future...
[ Renji: Wait... did anyone else see that? A Guild? Someone actually created one already?! ]
[ Connie: Yeah, it popped up in the announcements. First Guild... Codebreakers... Cool name. I’m going to name mine with Hunters... So they will call us the Hunters Guild. ]
[ Tomas: Codebreakers Guild... Leader: Kai. So that’s the guy. Damn, he beat everyone to it. ]
[ Eliza: What does a Guild even do? Is it just a fancy team name, or are there real features? ]
[ Renji: Who knows. Maybe they can occupy a land or something? It won’t be surprising at this point. ]
[ Connie: I guess the strongest Guild will dominate resources. ]
[ Tomas: I bet more Guilds will pop up soon. No one wants to be left behind now. ]

[ Sharmaine: The world just changed again. Guilds are going to reshape everything. Still, my shelter is busy prepping for the Surveillance Sweep. Let’s focus on that Event first. We’re going underground, baby! ]

chapters.title: Chapter 185: Preparing both Shelters and Slow Upgrade
paragraphs: Sharmaine’s decision to share their plan wasn’t random. She also wanted to know about the others’ plans. As expected, several other Survivors immediately reacted.

[ Owen: Underground? I don’t know... hiding might work at first, but drones scan wide areas. If they catch even one signal, the hunter bots will swarm, and no escape route. They’ll smoke you out, bruh. Maybe you should be preparing to fight instead of just hiding. ]

[ Ralph: I disagree. Fighting drones head‐on is suicide unless you’ve got Augmented Humans on your side or if you have strong warrior-class Survivors... Anyway, I think shelters that stay quiet and minimize exposure will last longer. Going underground is the safest bet. ]

[ Joseph: Both of you make sense. The Sweep lasts seven days. We can’t fight nonstop, but we can’t hide forever either. Maybe the best plan is to rotate... stay hidden most of the time, then strike when drones get too close. ]
[ Owen: That’s risky, but it might be the only way. If we just sit underground, we’ll starve or run out of supplies. ]

[ Ralph: Supplies don’t matter if you’re dead. Survive the Sweep first, then worry about food. You’re all high level... You can survive a few days without eating. Just prep some nuts, leaves, or something. ]
[ Joseph: Either way, this Event is going to test everyone. Survivors that can adapt fast will live. Those that don’t... well, the Swarmers will clean them out. ]
In the meantime, after a brief conversation with his team, Kai wasted no time.
He invited the other Survivors from Earth to join his Guild. The matters of the Guild Missions would be handled by them.
For now, they had to take the Global Event’s matter seriously.
For seven days, drones and swarmers would be sweeping across the regions. They only had five days to prepare.
The first step was fortification.
Windows were blocked with steel sheets scavenged from the warehouse. Every opening was sealed, leaving only narrow slits for observation...
Just like that, the workers hammered, and if they could weld, they might’ve started already.
It was quite tiring, but they had to do this...
Soon, traps were also laid around the perimeter... tripwires connected to cans and scrap metal that rattled loudly when triggered.
Well, it was definitely a substandard method, but it might work...
Then, there were also sharpened stakes hidden beneath loose soil, and barricades designed to funnel drones into narrow paths.
Even Amer, their cook, helped with this as he worked tirelessly, setting up reinforced barriers and layering wooden spikes along choke points with Jonas and the others.

Aurora and Claire handled the jammers, testing their range and adjusting frequencies. They weren’t entirely sure how effective they would be, but the belief was that disrupting signals could also interfere with the Swarmers’ ability to detect human presence. Whether it was true or not, it was still better to deploy them than risk being scanned without protection.
Kai’s A‐Grade Sentinel, Atom, just stood at the gate of the shelter, scanning for vulnerabilities. Well, they weren’t sure about Atom’s battery after all...
Still, Kai’s mind was torn.
Haven‐45 had artillery, a larger defensive perimeter, and the forest nearby for cover. It was the ideal stronghold. If all Guild fighters gathered there, defense would be easier.
But Freedom Shelter was equally important. It had a field of crops that Aurora was developing...
Furthermore, if they abandoned it, Angelo could occupy it, and reclaiming it later would be really difficult.
In the end, Kai made his decision.
He would stay at Freedom Shelter with Atom, Amer, Jonas, Aurora, Mei, and the workers. They would hold this ground.
Claire and Russel, however, were sent to Haven‐45. Not because Kai didn’t want to protect Claire, but because she was strong enough to protect others. He trusted her to lead the defense there.
The next day, Kai joined them on the return trip... It was also for resupplying Haven‐45 with his Gift Packs.
Riding alongside Claire and Russel on their bikes, he checked his system notifications.
[ Upgrade in Progress... Estimated Completion: 6 Hours ]
What he was looking at right now was the Talent Upgrade Crystal’s effect.
Apparently, after using it last night, he actually had to wait for 15 hours to complete the process!
He really thought that it was instantaneous like before.
In any case, that was also the reason why he was here... Instead of waiting idly, he chose to move with Claire and Russel.
The ride back to Haven‐45 was rough, but when Kai finally saw the towering artillery sticking out above the shelter walls, he couldn’t help but pause...
The weapon looked imposing under the sun. It wasn’t just a deterrent... It showed how New Haven‐45 was no ordinary shelter.
"Looks neat..."
As soon as they approached the gates, Kai was greeted by a familiar figure.
Ralph stood tall in the wooden watchtower, waving his hand down at them. "Welcome back!" he called.
Inside, Kai immediately noticed that not much had changed.
Then, he scanned the area and quickly noticed something else. The wandering merchant, Jyrus, had already left. No trace of his cart anymore...
Anyway, the only major difference was the artillery’s position, shifted slightly to cover a wider angle of fire. It was a smart adjustment.
Victor, Wallace, Elena, Marissa, Farrah, and Alfie quickly gathered around... They all looked excited.
Kai was confused at first since he had never been welcomed like this before.
However, he soon realized what was going on.
"Kai!" Victor started. "We heard about the Guild. We want in. All of us. Please invite us!"
Ralph chuckled... "Yeah. We’ve been talking. We don’t want to be left behind. No one’s planning to make another Guild... Let us join you."
Kai couldn’t help but laugh after hearing this. He planned to do that anyway.
"Hahaha! Of course, I’ll invite you all."
Just like that, everyone accepted Kai’s invite, and he was flooded with notifications.
[ Victor has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Ralph has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Farrah has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Alfie has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
"Everyone... Welcome to Codebreakers Guild!" Kai finally said as the group celebrated.
They even asked if they could brag about it in the World Chat...
However, as Kai planned to visit the warehouse, he soon realized something... All of them were actually carrying the same type of sword!
"This..."

sentences.text: Sharmaine’s decision to share their plan wasn’t random.
She also wanted to know about the others’ plans.
As expected, several other Survivors immediately reacted.
[ Owen: Underground?
I don’t know... hiding might work at first, but drones scan wide areas.
If they catch even one signal, the hunter bots will swarm, and no escape route.
They’ll smoke you out, bruh.
Maybe you should be preparing to fight instead of just hiding. ]
[ Ralph: I disagree.
Fighting drones head‐on is suicide unless you’ve got Augmented Humans on your side or if you have strong warrior-class Survivors...
Anyway, I think shelters that stay quiet and minimize exposure will last longer.
Going underground is the safest bet. ]
[ Joseph: Both of you make sense.
The Sweep lasts seven days.
We can’t fight nonstop, but we can’t hide forever either.
Maybe the best plan is to rotate... stay hidden most of the time, then strike when drones get too close. ]
[ Owen: That’s risky, but it might be the only way.
If we just sit underground, we’ll starve or run out of supplies. ]
[ Ralph: Supplies don’t matter if you’re dead.
Survive the Sweep first, then worry about food.
You’re all high level...
You can survive a few days without eating.
Just prep some nuts, leaves, or something. ]
[ Joseph: Either way, this Event is going to test everyone.
Survivors that can adapt fast will live.
Those that don’t... well, the Swarmers will clean them out. ]
In the meantime, after a brief conversation with his team, Kai wasted no time.
He invited the other Survivors from Earth to join his Guild.
The matters of the Guild Missions would be handled by them.
For now, they had to take the Global Event’s matter seriously.
For seven days, drones and swarmers would be sweeping across the regions.
They only had five days to prepare.
The first step was fortification.
Windows were blocked with steel sheets scavenged from the warehouse.
Every opening was sealed, leaving only narrow slits for observation...
Just like that, the workers hammered, and if they could weld, they might’ve started already.
It was quite tiring, but they had to do this...
Soon, traps were also laid around the perimeter... tripwires connected to cans and scrap metal that rattled loudly when triggered.
Well, it was definitely a substandard method, but it might work...
Then, there were also sharpened stakes hidden beneath loose soil, and barricades designed to funnel drones into narrow paths.
Even Amer, their cook, helped with this as he worked tirelessly, setting up reinforced barriers and layering wooden spikes along choke points with Jonas and the others.
Aurora and Claire handled the jammers, testing their range and adjusting frequencies.
They weren’t entirely sure how effective they would be, but the belief was that disrupting signals could also interfere with the Swarmers’ ability to detect human presence.
Whether it was true or not, it was still better to deploy them than risk being scanned without protection.
Kai’s A‐Grade Sentinel, Atom, just stood at the gate of the shelter, scanning for vulnerabilities.
Well, they weren’t sure about Atom’s battery after all...
Still, Kai’s mind was torn.
Haven‐45 had artillery, a larger defensive perimeter, and the forest nearby for cover.
It was the ideal stronghold.
If all Guild fighters gathered there, defense would be easier.
But Freedom Shelter was equally important.
It had a field of crops that Aurora was developing...
Furthermore, if they abandoned it, Angelo could occupy it, and reclaiming it later would be really difficult.
In the end, Kai made his decision.
He would stay at Freedom Shelter with Atom, Amer, Jonas, Aurora, Mei, and the workers.
They would hold this ground.
Claire and Russel, however, were sent to Haven‐45.
Not because Kai didn’t want to protect Claire, but because she was strong enough to protect others.
He trusted her to lead the defense there.
The next day, Kai joined them on the return trip...
It was also for resupplying Haven‐45 with his Gift Packs.
Riding alongside Claire and Russel on their bikes, he checked his system notifications.
[ Upgrade in Progress...
Estimated Completion: 6 Hours ]
What he was looking at right now was the Talent Upgrade Crystal’s effect.
Apparently, after using it last night, he actually had to wait for 15 hours to complete the process!
He really thought that it was instantaneous like before.
In any case, that was also the reason why he was here...
Instead of waiting idly, he chose to move with Claire and Russel.
The ride back to Haven‐45 was rough, but when Kai finally saw the towering artillery sticking out above the shelter walls, he couldn’t help but pause...
The weapon looked imposing under the sun.
It wasn’t just a deterrent...
It showed how New Haven‐45 was no ordinary shelter.
"Looks neat..."
As soon as they approached the gates, Kai was greeted by a familiar figure.
Ralph stood tall in the wooden watchtower, waving his hand down at them.
"Welcome back!" he called.
Inside, Kai immediately noticed that not much had changed.
Then, he scanned the area and quickly noticed something else.
The wandering merchant, Jyrus, had already left.
No trace of his cart anymore...
Anyway, the only major difference was the artillery’s position, shifted slightly to cover a wider angle of fire.
It was a smart adjustment.
Victor, Wallace, Elena, Marissa, Farrah, and Alfie quickly gathered around...
They all looked excited.
Kai was confused at first since he had never been welcomed like this before.
However, he soon realized what was going on.
"Kai!" Victor started.
"We heard about the Guild.
We want in.
All of us.
Please invite us!"
Ralph chuckled...
"Yeah.
We’ve been talking.
We don’t want to be left behind.
No one’s planning to make another Guild...
Let us join you."
Kai couldn’t help but laugh after hearing this.
He planned to do that anyway.
"Hahaha!
Of course, I’ll invite you all."
Just like that, everyone accepted Kai’s invite, and he was flooded with notifications.
[ Victor has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Ralph has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
